title: Forty commits authored by 'root@localhost'
summary: You worked on a fresh machine with no git identity configured. Fix the author on the commits that need it — with rebase for a few, with an env-filter for many — and set things up so it cannot happen again.
mental_model: Author and committer are baked into the commit object, so changing either means new commits and new shas. When a rewrite is too disruptive, `.mailmap` fixes the *display* without touching history at all.

steps.title: See the damage
steps.why: Three commits authored by root@localhost. Contribution graphs, blame, `shortlog` and any code-ownership tooling all read that field, so it matters beyond tidiness.
steps.expect: Three commits with the wrong identity, one correct.

verify.label: three commits carry the wrong author

steps.title: The no-rewrite option: mailmap
steps.why: `.mailmap` maps identities at display time. Every git command that shows an author honours it, and no sha changes. If the commits are already pushed, try this before reaching for a rewrite.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Map the root identity to a real one"

steps.expect: %aN and %aE — the mailmapped forms — now show the correct identity.

verify.label: mailmap fixes the displayed identity with no rewrite
verify.hint: write .mailmap mapping the canonical name to the bad email

steps.title: …but the raw commits are unchanged
steps.why: `%ae` is the raw field, `%aE` the mailmapped one. Tools that read the object directly — some forges included — still see root@localhost. If that matters, you need a rewrite.
steps.expect: The commit object still says root@localhost.

steps.title: Rewrite the author on every matching commit
steps.why: `--env-filter` runs per commit and can set the author and committer environment variables. Conditioning on the old email means only the affected commits change identity — though every commit after them still gets a new sha.

actions.run: git filter-branch --force --env-filter 'if [ "$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL" = "root@localhost" ]; then export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="Learner"; export GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="learner@shakha.local"; fi; if [ "$GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL" = "root@localhost" ]; then export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="Learner"; export GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="learner@shakha.local"; fi' -- --branches

steps.expect: Every commit now authored correctly, in the object itself.

verify.label: the raw author field is fixed in every commit
verify.hint: git filter-branch --env-filter, conditioned on the old email

steps.title: Clean up the backup refs
steps.why: Same as any filter-branch: the originals live under `refs/original` until you delete them. Until then `git log --all` still shows the old identities.
commands: sh -c 'git for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" refs/original | xargs -n 1 git update-ref -d'

verify.label: no reference to the old identity remains anywhere

steps.title: The lighter tool for a handful of commits
steps.why: For three or four commits, `rebase --exec` with `--reset-author` avoids filter-branch entirely. It rewrites the same shas but is far easier to reason about and to abort.
steps.expect: Same result, achieved with a command you already understand.

verify.label: every commit now carries the correct identity

steps.title: Prevent the next occurrence
steps.why: `user.useConfigOnly true` makes git refuse to commit until an identity is configured, instead of inventing one from the hostname. Two config lines, and this whole scenario stops happening.

verify.label: git will now refuse to guess an identity
no commit anywhere is authored by root@localhost
verify.hint: filter-branch --env-filter, then delete refs/original and gc

verify.label: the mailmap is committed as the display-level safety net
every commit carries the correct author
git is configured to refuse a guessed identity in future

pitfalls: If the commits are pushed and shared, prefer `.mailmap`. A rewrite forces everyone to re-clone over a cosmetic field.
`--reset-author` also resets the author DATE to now. Use the env-filter approach when the original timestamps matter.
Author and committer are different fields. A rebase changes the committer and preserves the author — which is correct, and often surprises people reading `git log --format=%cn`.
`git config --global user.useConfigOnly true` is the real fix. Without it, git happily invents an identity from your username and hostname.
cheatsheet: fix the display with no rewrite
the lighter option for a few commits
